import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('/results/6_Nov_Optimised/gpt_4o/tool_calling/quenching/subtask_false/level_2/brief/sio2_quenching_2_trial_0/quench_data.csv')

# Plot density vs. temperature
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(data['Temp'], data['Density'], marker='o')
plt.xlabel('Temperature (K)')
plt.ylabel('Density (g/cm^3)')
plt.title('Density vs. Temperature')
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Calculate the derivative to find the change in slope
density_derivative = np.gradient(data['Density'], data['Temp'])

# Plot the derivative
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.plot(data['Temp'], density_derivative, marker='o')
plt.xlabel('Temperature (K)')
plt.ylabel('Derivative of Density')
plt.title('Derivative of Density vs. Temperature')
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()

# Identify the glass transition temperature (Tg)
# This is where the derivative changes significantly
Tg_index = np.argmax(np.abs(np.diff(density_derivative)))
Tg = data['Temp'].iloc[Tg_index]

print(f"Glass Transition Temperature (Tg): {Tg:.2f} K")
```

This code will plot the density versus temperature and its derivative, helping you visually identify the glass transition temperature where the slope changes. The `Tg` value is then printed out. Adjust the file path as necessary if you're running this in a different environment.
